findings.notes: Executive summary is the open-access Kidney Int 2024;105:684-701 article (Levin A et al.), hosted by KDIGO; downloaded via curl. KDIGO 2024 does NOT state a '2 of 3 samples over 3-6 months' rule — that formulation is ADA's (unverified here).

findings.assertion: KDIGO 2012 gave an explicit numeric repeat-testing rule for persistent albuminuria that KDIGO 2024 does not restate.
findings.value: Two or more positive tests (ACR ≥30 mg/g / ≥3 mg/mmol) on early-morning urine samples 1-2 weeks apart = persistent albuminuria
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2012 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of CKD; Kidney Int Suppl 2013;3:1-150. Figure 16 legend. SUPERSEDED by the 2024 edition.
findings.quote: Reagent strip device results should be confirmed using laboratory testing of the ACR on at least two further occasions. Patients with two or more positive (≥30 mg/g or ≥3 mg/mmol) tests on early morning samples 1-2 weeks apart should be diagnosed as having persistent albuminuria.
findings.notes: CSO decision needed: the 2024 guideline replaced this with a looser 'repeat / confirm on a first morning void' plus the 3-month chronicity rule. If MedSync encodes a numeric repeat protocol, it is drawing on a superseded edition and should say so. The same figure legend warns to consider transient causes (menstrual contamination, uncontrolled hypertension, symptomatic UTI, heart failure, strenuous exercise) and notes hematuria may indicate non-diabetic renal disease.

findings.assertion: KDIGO recommends assessing albuminuria and GFR at least annually in people with CKD, more often at higher risk of progression.
findings.value: At least 1×/year (adults: albuminuria; children: albuminuria/proteinuria) plus GFR
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Practice Points 2.1.1 and 2.1.2
findings.quote: Practice Point 2.1.1: Assess albuminuria in adults, or albuminuria/proteinuria in children, and GFR at least annually in people with CKD. Practice Point 2.1.2: Assess albuminuria and GFR more often for individuals at higher risk of CKD progression when measurement will impact therapeutic decisions.

findings.assertion: KDIGO gives a GFR × albuminuria monitoring-frequency grid (number of measurements per year).
findings.value: Times per year by G/A cell — G1 (≥90): A1 1 (screen), A2 1, A3 3. G2 (60-89): A1 1 (screen), A2 1, A3 3. G3a (45-59): A1 1, A2 2, A3 3. G3b (30-44): A1 2, A2 3, A3 3. G4 (15-29): A1 3, A2 3, A3 4+. G5 (<15): A1 4+, A2 4+, A3 4+. Albuminuria columns in this figure: A1 <30 mg/g (<3 mg/mmol), A2 30-299 mg/g (3-29 mg/mmol), A3 ≥300 mg/g (≥30 mg/mmol).
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Figure 13 (reproduced from the ADA/KDIGO 2022 consensus report, Kidney Int 2022;102:974-989)
findings.quote: Figure 13 | Frequency of monitoring glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and albuminuria in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD). … The numbers in the boxes are a guide to the frequency of monitoring (number of times per year).
findings.notes: CSO decision needed on how to render this as a rule. The G1/G2-A1 cells are labelled 'Screen', all others 'Treat'; the G4-A1 and G4-A2 cells carry an asterisk in the source figure whose footnote I could not resolve from the extracted text. Risk colouring: green = low risk (if no other markers of kidney disease, no CKD); yellow = moderately increased; orange = high; red = very high.

findings.assertion: KDIGO flags meaningful change on repeat testing (thresholds that exceed expected biological/analytical variability).
findings.value: eGFR change >20% on a subsequent test; eGFR reduction >30% after starting haemodynamically active therapy; doubling (≥2-fold increase) of ACR
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Practice Points 2.1.3, 2.1.4, 2.1.5
findings.quote: Practice Point 2.1.3: For people with CKD, a change in eGFR of >20% on a subsequent test exceeds the expected variability and warrants evaluation. … Practice Point 2.1.5: For albuminuria monitoring of people with CKD, a doubling of the ACR on a subsequent test exceeds laboratory variability and warrants evaluation.

findings.assertion: KDIGO gives an ordered preference list for albuminuria testing and explicitly permits reagent-strip and point-of-care pathways where laboratory access is limited.
findings.value: Preference order: (i) urine ACR; (ii) reagent-strip urinalysis for albumin and ACR with automated reading. If measuring protein: (i) PCR, (ii) reagent strip for total protein automated, (iii) reagent strip for total protein manual. POCT ACR devices should detect ≥85% of people with ACR ≥30 mg/g (≥3 mg/mmol).
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Practice Point 1.3.1.1, Recommendation 1.4.1 (2C), Practice Point 1.4.3
findings.quote: Recommendation 1.4.1: We suggest that point-of-care testing (POCT) may be used for creatinine and urine albumin measurement where access to a laboratory is limited or providing a test at the point-of-care facilitates the clinical pathway (2C). … Practice Point 1.4.3: … Assess the ability of the POCT ACR devices to produce a positive result in 85% of people with significant albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g or ≥3 mg/mmol)
findings.notes: Directly relevant to the Mulago/low-resource setting. The guideline body adds: 'We acknowledge that reagent strip devices can have a role in settings where access to laboratory services may be limited', and 'healthcare providers should tailor the evaluation of cause based on these resource constraints (e.g., urine protein reagent strip testing instead of ACR)'.

findings.assertion: KDIGO warns that total-protein reagent strips are insufficiently sensitive and must be confirmed by quantitative laboratory measurement expressed as a ratio to urine creatinine.
findings.value: Reagent-strip positive → confirm by quantitative lab ACR (or PCR); total-protein strips are semiquantitative, unstandardised between manufacturers, and do not adjust for urine concentration
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Practice Point 1.3.1.2 and Section 1.3 rationale
findings.quote: Commonly used reagent strip devices measuring total protein are insufficiently sensitive for the reliable detection of proteinuria, do not adjust for urinary concentration, and are only semiquantitative. Furthermore, there is no standardization between manufacturers. The use of such strips should be discouraged in favor of quantitative laboratory measurements of albuminuria or proteinuria, or validated point-of-care devices for urine albumin/ACR … When used, reagent strip results should be confirmed by laboratory testing.
findings.notes: CSO decision needed: this is a 'discouraged but permitted' pathway. A decision-support tool in a setting where ACR is genuinely unavailable must present the dipstick result as provisional, never as a stage.

findings.assertion: Where quantitative ACR is unavailable, KDIGO 2012 supplied an explicit protein-reagent-strip → albuminuria-category mapping (dropped from the 2024 edition).
findings.value: Protein reagent strip: negative to trace = A1; trace to '+' = A2; '+' or greater = A3. Corresponding PER: <150 / 150-500 / >500 mg/24 h. Corresponding PCR: <15 / 15-50 / >50 mg/mmol (SI) = <150 / 150-500 / >500 mg/g (conventional).
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2012 CKD Guideline, Table 7 and Recommendation 1.2.4. SUPERSEDED — no equivalent table appears in the 2024 edition.
findings.quote: Table 7 | Relationship among categories for albuminuria and proteinuria — Protein reagent strip: Normal to mildly increased (A1) Negative to trace; Moderately increased (A2) Trace to +; Severely increased (A3) + or greater. … 1.2.4: Assign albuminuria categories as follows [Table 6] … *note that where albuminuria measurement is not available, urine reagent strip results can be substituted (Table 7)
findings.notes: CSO decision REQUIRED before shipping. The same guideline warns the mapping is inexact: 'The relationship between urine reagent strip results and other measures depends on urine concentration', and elsewhere: an ACR ≥30 mg/g 'may sometimes be detectable as trace using a urine reagent strip, depending on urine concentration, but this is not a consistent finding until AER exceeds approximately 300 mg/24 hours (ACR ≥300 mg/g [≥30 mg/mmol])' — i.e. a protein dipstick will MISS most A2 albuminuria. KDIGO 2012 also notes PCR 'is insensitive in the detection of moderately increased albuminuria/proteinuria'.

findings.assertion: WHO PEN (primary-care, low-resource protocol) specifies annual proteinuria testing as the diabetes kidney-complication screen, with referral if positive.
findings.value: Test for proteinuria annually; refer to higher level of care if positive
findings.standardVersion: WHO package of essential noncommunicable (PEN) disease interventions for primary health care, 2020 (ISBN 978-92-4-000922-6), Module 2.2 Diabetes — Screening for chronic complications
findings.quote: Test for proteinuria annually – REFER to higher level of care if positive
findings.notes: Landing page: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240009226 (fetched; the IRIS bitstream URL is the PDF it links to). Same module: 'REFER for dilated-pupil retinal exam upon diagnosis and every 2 years thereafter, or as per ophthalmologist recommendation.' The PEN essential-equipment list includes both 'Urine protein test strips' and 'Urine microalbuminuria test strips'.

findings.assertion: WHO PEN's diabetes training manual states the ACR-unavailable fallback explicitly and gives referral criteria.
findings.value: Annual spot-urine ACR + serum creatinine (for eGFR); if ACR unavailable, test for proteinuria, preferably with strips that specifically measure lower concentrations of albumin; refer all patients with proteinuria, those with moderate albuminuria, and those with GFR <60 ml/min/1.73 m²
findings.standardVersion: Training manual: WHO Package of Essential NCD Interventions (PEN) — Management of Type 2 Diabetes (no version/date printed on the document)
findings.quote: Monitor the albumin/creatinine ratio in a spot urine sample and serum creatinine (for calculation of the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) once a year. … If measurement of the albumin/creatinine ratio is not available, test for proteinuria (preferably with strips that specifically measure lower concentrations of albumin). … Refer for specialist assessment all patients with proteinuria, those with moderate albuminuria and those with GFR<60 ml/min/1.73 m2
findings.notes: DO NOT ENCODE THIS DOCUMENT'S ACR CUT-OFF. The same page reads 'CKD is defined by GFR< OR the presence of moderate or severe albuminuria (albumin-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/mmol)' — the eGFR value is missing (an apparent typesetting loss) and ≥30 mg/mmol equals 300 mg/g, i.e. KDIGO's SEVERE (A3) threshold, not 'moderate'. See conflicts. The manual elsewhere correctly gives 'microalbuminuria: 30–300 mg/24 h, or an albumin/creatinine ratio 30–300 mg/g'.

findings.assertion: KDIGO gives albuminuria-based and eGFR-based criteria for referral to specialist kidney care.
findings.value: eGFR <30 ml/min per 1.73 m²; 5-year kidney-failure risk >3-5% by validated equation; consistent ACR ≥300 mg/g (≥30 mg/mmol) or AER ≥300 mg/24 h (≈ PCR ≥500 mg/g [≥50 mg/mmol]) in combination with haematuria; a consistent ACR >700 mg/g (>70 mg/mmol); ≥2-fold increase in albuminuria on monitoring; sustained fall in GFR >20% (or >30% on haemodynamically active therapy)
findings.standardVersion: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Figure 48 and Practice Point 2.2.1
findings.quote: Figure 48 | Circumstances for referral to specialist kidney care services … Consistent finding of significant albuminuria (ACR ≥300 mg/g [≥30 mg/mmol] or AER ≥300 mg/24 hours, approximately equivalent to PCR ≥500 mg/g [≥50 mg/mmol] or PER ≥500 mg/24 h) in combination with hematuria … A consistent finding of ACR >700 mg/g [>70 mg/mmol]
findings.notes: Note the ≥300 mg/g criterion in Figure 48 is qualified 'in combination with hematuria'; the unqualified albuminuria referral trigger is >700 mg/g (>70 mg/mmol).

findings.assertion: The International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) severity scale has five levels defined by findings on dilated ophthalmoscopy.
findings.value: No apparent retinopathy = no abnormalities. Mild NPDR = microaneurysms only. Moderate NPDR = more than just microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR. Severe NPDR (international definition, no signs of PDR) = any of: >20 intraretinal haemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants; definite venous beading in ≥2 quadrants; prominent IRMA in ≥1 quadrant. PDR = one or both of: neovascularisation; vitreous/preretinal haemorrhage.
findings.standardVersion: Adapted from Wilkinson CP, Ferris FL III, Klein RE, et al. Ophthalmology 2003;110:1677-1682, as reproduced in AAO Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern, approved 13 September 2024, Table 1
findings.quote: TABLE 1 DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DISEASE SEVERITY SCALE AND INTERNATIONAL CLINICAL DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DISEASE SEVERITY SCALE — No apparent retinopathy: No abnormalities. Mild NPDR: Microaneurysms only. Moderate NPDR: More than just microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR. Severe NPDR … International definition: Any of the following and no signs of proliferative retinopathy: • More than 20 intraretinal hemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants • Definite venous beading in 2 or more quadrants • Prominent IRMA in 1 or more quadrants. PDR: One or both of the following: • Neovascularization • Vitreous/preretinal hemorrhage
findings.notes: Landing page https://www.aao.org/education/preferred-practice-pattern/diabetic-retinopathy-ppp was fetched first; the quoted values were read in the linked PDF asset (URL given). This same table carries the US/ETDRS variant of severe NPDR — see conflicts.

findings.assertion: The US (ETDRS-derived) '4-2-1 rule' definition of severe NPDR uses standard-photograph severity rather than a haemorrhage count.
findings.value: Any of the following (4-2-1 rule) and no signs of proliferative retinopathy: severe intraretinal haemorrhages and microaneurysms (≥ ETDRS standard photograph 2A) in each of 4 quadrants; definite venous beading (≥ standard photograph 6A) in ≥2 quadrants; moderate IRMA (≥ standard photograph 8A) in ≥1 quadrant
findings.standardVersion: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024, Table 1 (US definition) and Glossary
findings.quote: Severe nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR): Using the 4-2-1 rule, the presence of at least one of the following features: (1) severe intraretinal hemorrhages and microaneurysms, equaling or exceeding standard photograph 2A, present in 4 quadrants; (2) venous beading in 2 or more quadrants (standard photograph 6A); or (3) moderate IRMA equaling or exceeding standard photograph 8A in 1 or more quadrants.
findings.notes: CSO decision needed: the US definition requires reference standard photographs that will not be available at a Ugandan district/ward screening point. The international '>20 intraretinal haemorrhages per quadrant' definition is the implementable one.

findings.assertion: Two or more severe-NPDR characteristics defines very severe NPDR.
findings.value: ≥2 of the severe NPDR (4-2-1) characteristics = very severe NPDR
findings.standardVersion: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024, Table 1 notes
findings.quote: Any patient with two or more of the characteristics of severe NPDR is considered to have very severe NPDR.
findings.notes: 'Very severe NPDR' is not one of the five ICDR levels; it is an ETDRS-derived qualifier retained in the AAO PPP.

findings.assertion: PDR is subdivided into high-risk and non-high-risk, with a defined disc-area threshold.
findings.value: High-risk PDR: new vessels on or within 1 disc diameter of the optic disc ≥ ETDRS standard photograph 10A (about one-quarter to one-third disc area), with or without vitreous/preretinal haemorrhage; OR vitreous and/or preretinal haemorrhage accompanied by new vessels (NVD < standard photo 10A, or NVE ≥ one-quarter disc area)
findings.standardVersion: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024, Appendix 5 Table A5-1 (ETDRS classification), adapted from ETDRS report number 7, Ophthalmology 1991;98:742
findings.quote: High-risk proliferative retinopathy … New vessels on or within 1 disc diameter of the optic disc ≥ standard photograph 10A* (about one-quarter to one-third disc area), with or without vitreous or preretinal hemorrhage; or vitreous and/or preretinal hemorrhage accompanied by new vessels, either new vessels at the optic disc < standard photograph 10A or new vessels elsewhere ≥ one-quarter disc area
findings.notes: The ICDR five-level scale does not itself split PDR; this split comes from ETDRS/DRS and drives urgency of PRP.

findings.assertion: The ICDR scale was derived from ETDRS and WESDR data and is explicitly not a replacement for ETDRS.
findings.value: Qualitative relationship: ICDR is a simplified, clinically usable condensation of the ETDRS staging system, developed by consensus (April 2002 workshop, International Congress of Ophthalmology; modified Delphi) and based on ETDRS + WESDR evidence
findings.standardVersion: American Academy of Ophthalmology clinical statement, 'International Clinical Classification System for Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema', May 2012 (summary document dated October 2002); Global Diabetic Retinopathy Project Task Force
findings.quote: Although the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) staging system is recognized as the gold standard for grading in clinical trials, in everyday clinical practice, it has not proven to be easy or practical to use. There are too many levels … This would not replace the ETDRS, but provide a common, user-friendly terminology to describe disease severity and risk of progression categories.
findings.notes: Both the HTML page and its linked PDF (https://www.aao.org/Assets/3d3ce31b-39cf-444e-b393-1ae0ca8bfcf9/634965436738770000/sum-clinical-dr-and-dme-pdf) were fetched and read. Neither carries the severity tables themselves — only the rationale — which is why the ICDR table above is cited to the AAO PPP instead.

findings.assertion: The ETDRS classification levels themselves (for cross-referencing an ICDR grade to a trial-grade stage).
findings.value: Mild NPDR = ≥1 microaneurysm and criteria for moderate not met. Moderate NPDR = haemorrhages and/or microaneurysms ≥ standard photograph 2A, and/or soft exudates, venous beading or IRMA definitely present, and severe not met. Severe NPDR = cotton wool spots + venous beading + IRMA all definitely present in ≥2 of fields 4-7; or 2 of those 3 in ≥2 of fields 4-7 with haemorrhages/microaneurysms in these 4 fields ≥ standard photo 2A in ≥1; or IRMA in each of fields 4-7 and ≥ standard photograph 8A in ≥2. Early PDR = new vessels, high-risk criteria not met. High-risk PDR = as above.
findings.standardVersion: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024, Appendix 5 Table A5-1; adapted from ETDRS report number 7, Ophthalmology 1991;98:742, with grading per ETDRS report number 10, Ophthalmology 1991;98:786-806
findings.quote: TABLE A5-1 CLASSIFICATION OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY IN THE EARLY TREATMENT OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY STUDY — Mild nonproliferative retinopathy: At least 1 microaneurysm, and definition not met for moderate nonproliferative retinopathy, severe nonproliferative retinopathy, early proliferative retinopathy, or high-risk proliferative retinopathy
findings.notes: ETDRS has no 'no apparent retinopathy' row in this table and depends on 7-field stereo photography (fields 4-7) plus reference standard photographs — not deliverable at a screening point. This is why ICDR exists.

findings.assertion: Diabetic macular oedema is graded separately from retinopathy severity, and current international classification uses centre involvement rather than the original 2003 mild/moderate/severe scale.
findings.value: No DME = no retinal thickening or hard exudates in the macula. Non-central-involved DME = retinal thickening in the macula that does not involve the central subfield zone (1 mm diameter). Central-involved DME = retinal thickening in the macula that does involve the central subfield zone (1 mm diameter).
findings.standardVersion: International Council of Ophthalmology, ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care, updated 2017 (© ICO January 2017), Table 1
findings.quote: Diabetic macular edema (DME) is an additional important complication that is assessed separately from the stages of retinopathy, as it can be found in eyes at any DR severity level and can run an independent course. Currently, diabetic eyes are generally classified as having no DME, noncentral-involved DME, or central-involved DME. … Noncentral-involved DME: Retinal thickening in the macula that does not involve the central subfield zone that is 1mm in diameter. Central-involved DME: Retinal thickening in the macula that does involve the central subfield zone that is 1mm in diameter
findings.notes: SOURCING CAVEAT: ICO's own copy at https://icoph.org/mp-files/ico-guidelines-for-diabetic-eye-care.pdf/ is behind a MemberPress login and returns an HTML paywall page, not the PDF. The document read is the genuine ICO PDF (every page footer reads 'International Council of Ophthalmology | Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care | Page N — Copyright © ICO January 2017') hosted by the Vitreo-Retina Society of the Philippines. CSO should confirm against an ICO-hosted copy before shipping. Table footnote: 'Hard exudates are a sign of current or previous macular edema. DME is defined as retinal thickening, and this requires a three-dimensional assessment that is best performed by a dilated examination using slit-lamp biomicroscopy and/or stereo fundus photography.' The AAO PPP 2024 uses the same CI-DME / NCI-DME split.

findings.assertion: AAO recommends when to start retinal screening and the interval in the absence of retinopathy.
findings.value: Type 1 diabetes: first exam 5 years after diagnosis, then yearly. Type 2 diabetes: first exam at time of diagnosis, then yearly. Pregnancy (pre-existing type 1 or type 2): soon after conception and early in the first trimester; then no retinopathy to mild/moderate NPDR every 3-12 months, severe NPDR or worse every 1-3 months. Gestational diabetes does not require an eye examination during pregnancy.
findings.standardVersion: American Academy of Ophthalmology, Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern, approved 13 September 2024, Table 2
findings.quote: TABLE 2 RECOMMENDED EYE EXAMINATIONS FOR PATIENTS WITH DIABETES MELLITUS AND NO DIABETIC RETINOPATHY — Type 1: 5 years after diagnosis / Yearly. Type 2: At time of diagnosis / Yearly. Pregnancy (type 1 or type 2): Soon after conception and early in the first trimester; • No retinopathy to mild or moderate NPDR: every 3–12 months • Severe NPDR or worse: every 1–3 months. … ‡ Women who develop gestational diabetes do not require an eye examination during pregnancy
findings.notes: Also stated in the body: 'Individuals with type 2 diabetes without DR should have an annual dilated eye examination'; 'Individuals with type 1 diabetes without DR should have annual dilated eye examinations beginning 5 years after the onset of diabetes.' Footnote: 'Pubertal patients require increased vigilance due to increased risk of progression.'

findings.assertion: ICO gives resource-stratified re-examination and referral intervals keyed to the ICDR grade — the low/intermediate-resource column is the one relevant to a Ugandan district setting.
findings.value: HIGH-RESOURCE (Table 2a): no apparent DR / mild NPDR with no DME — re-examine 1-2 years, referral not required; mild NPDR — 6-12 months, referral not required; moderate NPDR — 3-6 months, referral required; severe NPDR — <3 months, referral required; PDR — <1 month, referral required; non-central-involved DME — 3 months, referral required; central-involved DME — 1 month, referral required. LOW/INTERMEDIATE-RESOURCE (Table 2b): no apparent DR / mild NPDR with no DME — 1-2 years, no referral; mild NPDR — 1-2 years, no referral; moderate NPDR — 6-12 months, referral required; severe NPDR — <3 months, referral required; PDR — <1 month, referral required; non-central-involved DME — 3 months, referral not required (recommended if laser resources available); central-involved DME — 1 month, referral required.
findings.standardVersion: ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care, updated 2017, Tables 2a and 2b
findings.quote: Table 2b. Re-examination and Referral Recommendations Based on Simplified Classification of Diabetic Retinopathy* and Diabetic Macular Edema for Low-/Intermediate Resource Settings. … Moderate nonproliferative DR 6-12 months Referral required; Severe nonproliferative DR < 3 months Referral required; PDR < 1 month Referral required … * In cases where diabetes is controlled.
findings.notes: Internal inconsistency in the source: both tables list 'No apparent DR, mild nonproliferative DR and no DME: 1-2 year' immediately followed by a separate 'Mild nonproliferative DR' row (6-12 months in 2a, 1-2 years in 2b). CSO must decide which applies to mild NPDR in the high-resource pathway. Same caveat about the mirrored host as the DME finding. ICO's post-treatment/ophthalmologist follow-up schedule (Tables 3a/3b) differs again: e.g. non-central-involved DME 3-6 months, central-involved DME 1-3 months, stable treated PDR 6-12 months.

findings.assertion: AAO gives follow-up intervals by combined retinopathy severity and DME status.
findings.value: Months to follow-up (no DME / non-centre-involved DME / centre-involved DME): No apparent retinopathy 12 / – / –. Mild NPDR 12 / 3-6 / 1. Moderate NPDR 6-12 / 3-6 / 1. Severe NPDR 3-4 / 2-4 / 1. Non-high-risk PDR 3-4 / 2-4 / 1. High-risk PDR 2-4 / 2-4 / 1.
findings.standardVersion: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy Preferred Practice Pattern 2024, Table 5
findings.quote: TABLE 5 INITIAL MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR PATIENTS WITH DIABETES — Severity of Retinopathy / Presence of Macular Edema / Follow-up (Months): No apparent retinopathy No 12; Mild NPDR No 12, NCI-DME 3–6, CI-DME 1; Moderate NPDR No 6–12, NCI-DME 3–6, CI-DME 1; Severe NPDR No 3–4, NCI-DME 2–4, CI-DME 1; Non-high-risk PDR No 3–4 …; High-risk PDR No 2–4 …
findings.notes: The CI-DME '1 month' entries carry an asterisk: 'Treatments that may be considered included intravitreal corticosteroids or anti-VEGF agents.' High-risk PDR: PRP 'Recommended' in all three DME strata.

findings.assertion: WHO PEN specifies the primary-care retinopathy screening interval for low-resource settings.
findings.value: Dilated-pupil retinal exam at diagnosis, then every 2 years (biennially) thereafter, or as per ophthalmologist recommendation
findings.standardVersion: WHO PEN 2020, Module 2.2 Diabetes; and WHO PEN Training Manual: Management of Type 2 Diabetes
findings.quote: REFER for dilated-pupil retinal exam upon diagnosis and every 2 years thereafter, or as per ophthalmologist recommendation
findings.notes: The training manual adds: 'People with type 2 diabetes should be screened for retinopathy by a trained person upon diagnosis and biennially thereafter … Patients reporting vision loss at any visit and those who have not had a retinal exam in more than 2 years should be referred to an ophthalmologist.' This is the loosest of the three intervals — see conflicts.

conflicts.assertion: Definition of severe NPDR — haemorrhage criterion
positions: ICDR international definition (AAO PPP 2024 Table 1; Wilkinson 2003; ICO 2017 Table 1): 'More than 20 intraretinal hemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants' / '(≥20 in each quadrant)', plus definite venous beading in 2 quadrants, plus 'prominent' (ICO: unqualified) IRMA in 1 quadrant.

US / ETDRS 4-2-1 definition (AAO PPP 2024 Table 1, US definition and Glossary): 'Severe intraretinal hemorrhages and microaneurysms in each of 4 quadrants' judged against ETDRS standard photograph 2A, venous beading against standard photograph 6A, and 'moderate' IRMA against standard photograph 8A.

ICO 2017 differs again in wording from AAO's rendering of the international definition: ICO lists IRMA 'in 1 quadrant' without the qualifier 'prominent', and frames all three as modifiers of moderate NPDR.
conflicts.recommendation: Encode the ICDR INTERNATIONAL definition (>20 intraretinal haemorrhages per quadrant in each of 4 quadrants; definite venous beading in ≥2 quadrants; prominent IRMA in ≥1 quadrant). It is countable at the point of care and does not require ETDRS reference standard photographs, which will not exist at a Ugandan screening site. Surface the US 4-2-1 phrasing only as an explanatory alias, never as the operative test. CSO sign-off required on whether to require the word 'prominent' for IRMA, since AAO and ICO differ.

conflicts.assertion: Retinopathy screening interval for a person with diabetes and no apparent retinopathy
positions: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024, Table 2: yearly (type 1 from 5 years after diagnosis; type 2 from diagnosis). The PPP body argues against biennial screening, citing English Diabetic Eye Screening Programme data that biennial screening 'would have delayed detection of sight-threatening DR for 56.3% of patients and PDR for 43.6% of patients by 1 year, especially among Black patients.'
ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care 2017, Tables 2a/2b and 3a/3b: 're-examination in 1-2 years' for no apparent DR, in BOTH high-resource and low/intermediate-resource settings.
WHO PEN 2020 and the PEN training manual: dilated retinal exam at diagnosis and every 2 years thereafter.
conflicts.recommendation: Do not pick one silently. Make the interval a configurable clinical policy with an explicit default and show the source. For a Mulago/Uganda beachhead the ICO low-resource pathway (1-2 years) and WHO PEN (2 years) are the operationally realistic anchors, but the AAO/English-programme evidence of delayed detection — with a specifically noted excess harm in Black patients — is directly relevant to this population and argues for annual screening where capacity allows. This needs CSO adjudication before any default is shipped.

conflicts.assertion: Upper boundary of albuminuria category A2 / lower boundary of A3
positions: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Table 3 (and the identical KDIGO 2012 Table 6): A2 = 30-300 mg/g (3-30 mg/mmol); A3 = >300 mg/g (>30 mg/mmol).
KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Figure 13 (reproduced from the ADA/KDIGO 2022 consensus report): A2 = 30-299 mg/g (3-29 mg/mmol); A3 = ≥300 mg/g (≥30 mg/mmol).
conflicts.recommendation: Implement the A3 boundary as ACR ≥300 mg/g (≥30 mg/mmol) — i.e. the Figure 13 / ADA-KDIGO rendering — because it is unambiguous and leaves no gap, whereas Table 3's '30-300' and '>300' both claim exactly 300. Document the deviation from Table 3 and get CSO sign-off. A value of exactly 300 mg/g must never fall through to 'uncategorised'.

conflicts.assertion: ACR threshold for 'moderate' albuminuria in the WHO PEN training manual
positions: KDIGO 2024 (Table 3) and KDIGO 2012 (Table 6): moderately increased albuminuria (A2) = ACR 3-30 mg/mmol = 30-300 mg/g; severely increased (A3) = >30 mg/mmol = >300 mg/g.

WHO PEN training manual (Management of Type 2 Diabetes), Diabetic kidney disease section: 'CKD is defined by GFR< OR the presence of moderate or severe albuminuria (albumin-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/mmol).' The eGFR figure is missing from the sentence, and ≥30 mg/mmol equals 300 mg/g — KDIGO's SEVERE threshold, not moderate.
The same WHO training manual, elsewhere: 'microalbuminuria: 30–300 mg/24 h, or an albumin/creatinine ratio 30–300 mg/g' — which agrees with KDIGO.
conflicts.recommendation: Treat the '≥30 mg/mmol' sentence as an error in the WHO document (a mg/g→mg/mmol unit slip, alongside a dropped eGFR value) and DO NOT encode it. Use KDIGO: A2 from ACR ≥3 mg/mmol (≥30 mg/g). Encoding 30 mg/mmol as the moderate-albuminuria trigger would miss the entire A2 band — exactly the patients diabetic-kidney-disease screening exists to find. Flag to the CSO explicitly.

conflicts.assertion: How many repeat samples confirm persistent albuminuria, and over what interval
positions: KDIGO 2024 (Practice Points 1.1.1.2, 1.1.3.1, 1.3.1.2): repeat tests to confirm; confirm an ACR ≥30 mg/g (≥3 mg/mmol) found on a random untimed urine with a subsequent first-morning-void midstream sample; chronicity requires a minimum of 3 months. No sample count is given.

KDIGO 2012 (Figure 16 legend, superseded): confirm reagent-strip results by laboratory ACR 'on at least two further occasions'; 'two or more positive (≥30 mg/g or ≥3 mg/mmol) tests on early morning samples 1-2 weeks apart' = persistent albuminuria.
ADA Standards of Care (widely cited '2 of 3 UACR specimens abnormal within a 3- to 6-month period') — NOT verified here; diabetesjournals.org returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt.
conflicts.recommendation: Encode the KDIGO 2024 rule as the operative one (repeat, confirm on a first morning void, and require ≥3 months' duration before labelling CKD), and cite KDIGO 2012's 'two positive early-morning samples 1-2 weeks apart' only as an explanatory sub-protocol marked as coming from a superseded edition. Do NOT encode the ADA 2-of-3 rule until someone with journal access verifies it against the current ADA Standards of Care — see unverifiable.

conflicts.assertion: Whether reagent-strip proteinuria may substitute for quantitative ACR
positions: KDIGO 2024: strips are permitted where laboratory access is limited (Recommendation 1.4.1, 2C, for POCT; Practice Point 1.3.1.1 lists automated-read strips second in preference), but 'The use of such strips should be discouraged in favor of quantitative laboratory measurements … When used, reagent strip results should be confirmed by laboratory testing.' No strip-to-category mapping table is provided.

KDIGO 2012, Recommendation 1.2.4 footnote and Table 7: 'where albuminuria measurement is not available, urine reagent strip results can be substituted', with an explicit mapping — negative to trace = A1, trace to '+' = A2, '+' or greater = A3.

WHO PEN 2020 / PEN training manual: annual proteinuria test as the primary-care screen; 'If measurement of the albumin/creatinine ratio is not available, test for proteinuria (preferably with strips that specifically measure lower concentrations of albumin).'
conflicts.recommendation: Ship the dipstick pathway as a screening-and-refer pathway only, never as a staging pathway. Present a positive strip as 'possible albuminuria — quantitative ACR required to stage', per WHO PEN's refer-if-positive rule, and carry KDIGO 2012's own warning that a total-protein strip will not reliably detect albuminuria until ACR approaches 300 mg/g (30 mg/mmol) — so a negative strip does NOT exclude A2. If MedSync surfaces the KDIGO 2012 strip-to-A-category mapping at all, it must be labelled as a superseded, approximate, urine-concentration-dependent aid. CSO sign-off required.

unverifiable: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 11 (Chronic Kidney Disease and Risk Management): every fetch attempt to diabetesjournals.org returned HTTP 403 (article HTML and article PDF, via both WebFetch and curl with a browser user-agent). This means I could NOT verify from primary source: (a) the '2 of 3 UACR specimens collected within a 3- to 6-month period should be abnormal' confirmation rule; (b) the recommendation to assess UACR and eGFR at least annually in type 1 diabetes of ≥5 years duration and in all type 2 diabetes; (c) ADA's UACR thresholds. I recall these from memory and they are widely cited, but no value above is attributed to ADA and none should be encoded on my say-so.

The frequently repeated claim that the ICDR scale 'condenses the 14 severity levels of the ETDRS scale into 5' — the specific number 14 appeared only in a search-results snippet of a secondary review, not in any primary document I retrieved. The AAO's own 2012 statement says only 'There are too many levels'.

The numeric ETDRS level codes (10 / 20 / 35 / 43 / 47 / 53 / 61 / 65 / 71 / 75 / 81 / 85) and their mapping onto the five ICDR categories. Neither the AAO clinical statement, the AAO PPP Appendix 5, nor the ICO 2017 guideline gives such a crosswalk. Do not fabricate one.

The ORIGINAL 2003 ICDR diabetic macular oedema severity scale (DME apparently absent / apparently present; and if present, mild / moderate / severe graded by how close retinal thickening and hard exudates lie to the centre of the macula). I did not retrieve Wilkinson 2003 itself (Ophthalmology, paywalled). The DME classification reported above is the current ICO 2017 no-DME / non-centre-involved / centre-involved scheme, which supersedes it in practice — but the historical three-tier wording is unverified.

The ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care were read from a professional-society mirror (vrsp.org.ph), because ICO's own file URL (icoph.org/mp-files/ico-guidelines-for-diabetic-eye-care.pdf/) sits behind a MemberPress login and returns an HTML paywall page rather than the PDF. The document is internally self-identifying as the genuine ICO 2017 guideline on every page, but I could not confirm it against an ICO-hosted copy.
Whether a diabetic-eye-care guideline newer than the ICO's 2017 update exists. I did not establish that 2017 is still ICO's current version.

Any KDIGO statement on WHEN to START kidney screening in diabetes by diabetes type (e.g. type 1 at 5 years, type 2 at diagnosis). Neither the KDIGO 2024 CKD guideline nor the KDIGO 2022 Diabetes Management in CKD guideline stated this in the sections I read; KDIGO's guidance is framed as 'test people at risk' plus 'at least annually in people with CKD'. That onset rule is ADA's, and ADA was unfetchable.

The footnote behind the asterisks on the G4/A1 and G4/A2 cells of KDIGO 2024 Figure 13 ('Treat*'). The marker survived text extraction from the PDF but its explanatory footnote did not, so the qualifier attached to those two monitoring frequencies is unknown to me.

Whether KDIGO 2024 anywhere restores a reagent-strip-to-albuminuria-category equivalence table. I grepped the full guideline for 'trace', '1+', 'approximate equivalent' and found none — the KDIGO 2012 Table 7 mapping appears to have been dropped rather than updated. I cannot rule out that it survives in a supplementary table I did not retrieve.

The publication date, version, and current status of the WHO PEN 'Training manual: Management of Type 2 Diabetes'. No date appears on the pages I read, and it is served from a who.int/docs path rather than the IRIS repository, so I cannot confirm it is current or that its unit error has not since been corrected.

Any Uganda Ministry of Health national guideline for diabetic kidney disease or retinopathy screening. I did not search for one, and it may set intervals or pathways that differ from all three international sources above. This should be checked before MedSync ships defaults for Mulago.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 GFR categories G1 ≥90; G2 60-89; G3a 45-59; G3b 30-44; G4 15-29; G5 <15 ml/min/1.73 m² (KDIGO 2024 Table 2)
audit.reason: URL fetched by me via curl: HTTP 200, 5,966,902-byte PDF (WebFetch gets 403 from kdigo.org's WAF, but the document is real). Extracted p.S137: 'Table 2| GFR categories in CKD — G1 ≥90 Normal or high; G2 60–89 Mildly decreased; G3a 45–59 Mildly to moderately decreased; G3b 30–44 Moderately to severely decreased; G4 15–29 Severely decreased; G5 <15 Kidney failure.' Page footer confirms citation 'Kidney International (2024) 105 (Suppl 4S), S117–S314'. Table number, values and journal citation all correct. The note that eGFR has no dual SI/conventional unit is correct.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 albuminuria categories A1 <30 mg/g (<3 mg/mmol), A2 30-300 mg/g (3-30 mg/mmol), A3 >300 mg/g (>30 mg/mmol); AER <30 / 30-300 / >300 mg/24h (Table 3, identical to KDIGO 2012 Table 6)
audit.reason: KDIGO 2024 p.S137: 'Table 3| Albuminuria categories in chronic kidney disease — A1 <30 (AER) / <3 mg/mmol / <30 mg/g Normal to mildly increased; A2 30–300 / 3–30 / 30–300 Moderately increased; A3 >300 / >30 / >300 Severely increased.' Cross-reference also verified: I extracted KDIGO_2012_CKD_GL.pdf (HTTP 200, 4,548,193 bytes) and its Table 6 is indeed titled 'Albuminuria categories in CKD' with identical values. Both the values and the 2012 table number are correct.

audit.assertion: CKD = kidney abnormality ≥3 months; albuminuria marker at ACR ≥30 mg/g (≥3 mg/mmol); decreased GFR <60 ml/min/1.73 m² (KDIGO 2024 Table 1)
audit.reason: KDIGO 2024 p.S137 verbatim: 'Table 1| Criteria for chronic kidney disease (either of the following present for a minimum of 3 months) — Markers of kidney damage (1 or more): Albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g [≥3 mg/mmol])... Decreased GFR: GFR <60 ml/min per 1.73 m2 (GFR categories G3a–G5).' Exact match including the G3a–G5 parenthetical.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 confirmation rule: repeat incidental abnormal ACR; confirm ACR ≥30 mg/g on random untimed urine with subsequent first-morning-void midstream sample; chronicity minimum 3 months (PP 1.1.1.2, 1.1.3.1, 1.1.3.2, 1.3.1.2)
audit.reason: Cited URL independently fetched: HTTP 200, 889,463-byte PDF, confirmed to be Levin A et al., 'Executive summary of the KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline... known knowns and known unknowns'. All four practice points present and verbatim in both the exec summary and the full guideline. PP 1.3.1.2 reads exactly: 'Confirm ACR ≥30 mg/g (≥3 mg/mmol) on a random untimed urine with a subsequent first morning void in the morning midstream urine sample.' PP 1.1.3.1: 'Proof of chronicity (duration of a minimum of 3 months)...'. PP 1.1.1.2 and 1.1.3.2 also match. Practice-point numbering is correct.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2012: two or more positive tests (ACR ≥30 mg/g / ≥3 mg/mmol) on early-morning urine samples 1-2 weeks apart = persistent albuminuria (Figure 16 legend; superseded by 2024)
audit.reason: KDIGO_2012_CKD_GL.pdf fetched by me (HTTP 200). Figure 16 legend verbatim: 'Patients with two or more positive (≥30 mg/g or ≥3 mg/mmol) tests on early morning samples 1-2 weeks apart should be diagnosed as having persistent albuminuria.' Figure number correct. The 'superseded' framing is fair: I grepped the 2024 full text and found no restatement of the 1-2-week numeric rule.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024: assess albuminuria (adults) or albuminuria/proteinuria (children) and GFR at least annually in people with CKD; more often at higher risk (PP 2.1.1, 2.1.2)
audit.reason: Verbatim in both the full guideline and the cited executive summary: 'Practice Point 2.1.1: Assess albuminuria in adults, or albuminuria/proteinuria in children, and GFR at least annually in people with CKD.' and 'Practice Point 2.1.2: Assess albuminuria and GFR more often for individuals at higher risk of CKD progression when measurement will impact therapeutic decisions.' Numbering correct.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 Figure 13 monitoring grid (times/year): G1 1/1/3; G2 1/1/3; G3a 1/2/3; G3b 2/3/3; G4 3/3/4+; G5 4+/4+/4+; reproduced from ADA/KDIGO 2022 (Kidney Int 2022;102:974-989)
audit.reason: I did not trust flattened PDF text order for a grid, so I re-extracted Figure 13 (page index 81, p.S197) with word-level coordinates. Rows by y-position: G1 (y≈170) Screen 1 | Treat 1 | Treat 3; G2 (y≈197) Screen 1 | Treat 1 | Treat 3; G3a (y≈226) 1 | 2 | 3; G3b (y≈253) 2 | 3 | 3; G4 (y≈282) Treat* 3 | Treat* 3 | Treat 4+; G5 (y≈308) 4+ | 4+ | 4+. Every one of the 18 cells matches. Column headers confirmed as '<30 mg/g / <3 mg/mmol', '30–299 mg/g / 3–29 mg/mmol', '≥300 mg/g / ≥30 mg/mmol'. Attribution verified verbatim in the legend: 'Reproduced from de Boer IH, Khunti K, Sadusky T, et al. ... Kidney Int. 2022;102:974–989.' Note the finding correctly flags that Figure 13's albuminuria bands (30–299 / ≥300) differ from Table 3's (30–300 / >300) — that inconsistency is genuinely present inside KDIGO 2024 itself, and the finding handled it honestly rather than silently harmonising.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 meaningful-change thresholds: eGFR change >20% on repeat; eGFR reduction >30% after haemodynamically active therapy; doubling of ACR (PP 2.1.3, 2.1.4, 2.1.5)
audit.reason: Verbatim: 'PP 2.1.3: For people with CKD, a change in eGFR of >20% on a subsequent test exceeds the expected variability and warrants evaluation.' 'PP 2.1.4: Among people with CKD who initiate hemodynamically active therapies, GFR reductions of >30% on subsequent testing exceed the expected variability...' 'PP 2.1.5: ... a doubling of the ACR on a subsequent test exceeds laboratory variability...'. All three numbers, all three practice-point numbers, and the pairing of each number to the right practice point are correct.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 albuminuria test preference order (ACR → automated albumin/ACR strip; protein: PCR → automated → manual strip); Rec 1.4.1 (2C) permits POCT; POCT ACR devices should detect ≥85% of people with ACR ≥30 mg/g
audit.reason: PP 1.3.1.1 preference order matches verbatim, including 'In all cases, a first void in the morning midstream sample is preferred'. Recommendation 1.4.1 grade verified as '(2C)' verbatim. CAVEAT on wording: PP 1.4.3 actually reads 'Assess the ability of the POCT ACR devices to produce a positive result in 85% of people with significant albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g or ≥3 mg/mmol)'. The guideline says 'in 85%', not '≥85%' — the finding adds an inequality the source does not carry. The number, the ACR threshold and the practice-point number are all correct; only the '≥' is an editorial addition with no clinical consequence.
audit.correctedValue: POCT ACR devices: assess ability to 'produce a positive result in 85% of people with significant albuminuria (ACR ≥30 mg/g or ≥3 mg/mmol)' — source says 'in 85%', not '≥85%'

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024: reagent-strip positive must be confirmed by quantitative lab measurement expressed as a ratio to urine creatinine; total-protein strips are semiquantitative, unstandardised between manufacturers, and do not adjust for urine concentration
audit.reason: Both halves verified. PP 1.3.1.2 bullet 1 verbatim: 'Confirm reagent strip positive albuminuria and/or proteinuria by quantitative laboratory measurement and express as a ratio to urine creatinine wherever possible (i.e., quantify the ACR or PCR if initial semiquantitative tests are positive).' Section 1.3 rationale (p.S191-2) verbatim: 'Commonly used reagent strip devices measuring total protein are insufficiently sensitive for the reliable detection of proteinuria, do not adjust for urinary concentration, and are only semiquantitative. Furthermore, there is no standardization between manufacturers.' This is an unusually exact paraphrase — all three descriptors are literally in the source.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2012 Table 7: protein reagent strip negative-to-trace = A1, trace-to-'+' = A2, '+' or greater = A3; PER <150 / 150-500 / >500 mg/24h; PCR <15 / 15-50 / >50 mg/mmol = <150 / 150-500 / >500 mg/g
audit.reason: KDIGO 2012 'Table 7 | Relationship among categories for albuminuria and proteinuria' extracted verbatim: PER <150 / 150–500 / >500; PCR (mg/mmol) <15 / 15–50 / >50; PCR (mg/g) <150 / 150–500 / >500; 'Protein reagent strip: Negative to trace | Trace to + | + or greater'. Recommendation 1.2.4 verified with its footnote '*note that where albuminuria measurement is not available, urine reagent strip results can be substituted (Table 7)'. The 'superseded / no equivalent in 2024' claim also checks out: grepping the 2024 full text for 'Protein reagent strip' returns no such mapping table.

audit.assertion: WHO PEN 2020 Module 2.2 Diabetes: test for proteinuria annually, refer to higher level of care if positive
audit.reason: URL fetched by me: HTTP 200, 2,584,724-byte PDF. Front matter confirms 'WHO package of essential noncommunicable (PEN) disease interventions for primary health care, ISBN 978-92-4-000922-6 (electronic version), © World Health Organization 2020' — ISBN and year exactly as cited. Page 25, section '2.2 DIABETES / SCREENING FOR CHRONIC COMPLICATIONS' verbatim: 'Test for proteinuria annually – REFER to higher level of care if positive.' Module number and section heading both correct.

audit.assertion: WHO PEN diabetes training manual: annual spot ACR + serum creatinine; if ACR unavailable test for proteinuria preferably with strips measuring lower albumin concentrations; refer all with proteinuria, moderate albuminuria, or GFR <60
audit.reason: URL fetched by me: HTTP 200, 1,947,397-byte, 35-page PDF titled 'Training manual — WHO Package of Essential NCD Interventions (PEN) Management of Type 2 Diabetes.' All three clauses verbatim: 'Monitor the albumin/creatinine ratio in a spot urine sample and serum creatinine (for calculation of the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) once a year.' / 'If measurement of the albumin/creatinine ratio is not available, test for proteinuria (preferably with strips that specifically measure lower concentrations of albumin).' / 'Refer for specialist assessment all patients with proteinuria, those with moderate albuminuria and those with GFR<60 ml/min/1.73 m2'. I also searched the document for a version/date and found none, so the finding's own 'no version/date printed' caveat is accurate. Separately worth flagging for the conflicts log: the same manual states 'CKD is defined by GFR< OR the presence of moderate or severe albuminuria (albumin-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/mmol)' — a truncated GFR value and a 10-fold unit error against KDIGO's ≥3 mg/mmol. That error is in WHO's document, not in this finding, but it means the manual should not be used as a threshold source.

audit.assertion: KDIGO 2024 Figure 48 referral criteria: eGFR <30; 5-yr KRT risk >3-5%; ACR ≥300 mg/g (≥30 mg/mmol) or AER ≥300 mg/24h (≈PCR ≥500 mg/g) with haematuria; ACR >700 mg/g (>70 mg/mmol); ≥2-fold albuminuria increase; GFR fall >20% (or >30% on haemodynamically active therapy)
audit.reason: Figure 48 (p.S255) extracted verbatim; every element matches, including the ones I most expected to be imported from NICE: 'A consistent finding of ACR >700 mg/g [>70 mg/mmol]' and 'Consistent finding of significant albuminuria (ACR ≥300 mg/g [≥30 mg/mmol] or AER ≥300 mg/24 hours, approximately equivalent to PCR ≥500 mg/g [≥50 mg/mmol] or PER ≥500 mg/24 h) in combination with hematuria'. Also verified: 'A >3%–5% 5-year risk of requiring KRT measured using a validated risk equation', 'eGFR <30 ml/min per 1.73 m2', 'A sustained fall in GFR of >20% or >30% in those people initiating hemodynamically active therapies', '≥2-fold increase in albuminuria...'. CAVEAT on citation completeness: Figure 48 is invoked by Practice Point 5.1.1 ('Refer adults with CKD to specialist kidney care services in the circumstances listed in Figure 48'), which the finding does not cite. PP 2.2.1 is real and does supply the 3%–5% criterion ('A 5-year kidney failure risk of 3%–5% can be used to determine need for nephrology referral'), so the citation is incomplete rather than wrong.
audit.correctedSource: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline, Figure 48 with Practice Point 5.1.1 (referral circumstances) and Practice Point 2.2.1 (3%–5% 5-year KRT risk)

audit.assertion: ICDR five-level severity scale (no apparent DR; mild NPDR = microaneurysms only; moderate; severe NPDR international definition >20 haemorrhages/4 quadrants, venous beading ≥2 quadrants, prominent IRMA ≥1 quadrant; PDR) — AAO DR PPP approved 13 Sept 2024, Table 1
audit.reason: URL fetched by me: HTTP 200, 1,460,297-byte PDF. Front matter verbatim: 'Approved by: Board of Trustees, September 13, 2024' — approval date exactly as cited. Table 1 (p.P92) extracted verbatim, international definition: 'More than 20 intraretinal hemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants; Definite venous beading in 2 or more quadrants; Prominent IRMA in 1 or more quadrants', with 'No apparent retinopathy / No abnormalities', 'Mild NPDR / Microaneurysms only', 'Moderate NPDR / More than just microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR', 'PDR / One or both of the following: Neovascularization; Vitreous/preretinal hemorrhage'. I independently checked the Wilkinson citation on PubMed (PMID 13129861): 'Ophthalmology 2003 Sep;110(9):1677-82' — the finding's page range is correct. (The PPP's own credit line cites p.1679, the table's page, which is not a discrepancy.)

audit.assertion: ETDRS-derived US '4-2-1' severe NPDR: haemorrhages/microaneurysms ≥ standard photo 2A in 4 quadrants; definite venous beading (≥ photo 6A) in ≥2 quadrants; moderate IRMA (≥ photo 8A) in ≥1 quadrant — AAO PPP 2024 Table 1 and Glossary
audit.reason: Correctly split across the two locations the finding names. Table 1 US definition verbatim: 'Any of the following (4-2-1 rule) and no signs of proliferative retinopathy: Severe intraretinal hemorrhages and microaneurysms in each of 4 quadrants; Definite venous beading in 2 or more quadrants; Moderate IRMA in 1 or more quadrants' — note Table 1 alone carries no photo numbers. The Glossary (p.P139) supplies them verbatim: 'Using the 4-2-1 rule... (1) severe intraretinal hemorrhages and microaneurysms, equaling or exceeding standard photograph 2A, present in 4 quadrants; (2) venous beading in 2 or more quadrants (standard photograph 6A); or (3) moderate IRMA equaling or exceeding standard photograph 8A in 1 or more quadrants.' Minor wording note: for venous beading the Glossary gives '(standard photograph 6A)' without an explicit '≥'; the finding writes '≥ standard photograph 6A'. The Glossary does describe 6A as 'less severe of two standards for venous beading', so the inequality is a defensible inference but is not literal source text.

audit.assertion: Two or more severe-NPDR (4-2-1) characteristics = very severe NPDR (AAO PPP 2024 Table 1 notes)
audit.reason: Table 1 NOTES verbatim: 'Any patient with two or more of the characteristics of severe NPDR is considered to have very severe NPDR.' Corroborated in the body text: 'defined as an eye with two or more of the 4-2-1 characteristics summarized in Table 1.' Located exactly where the finding says.

audit.assertion: High-risk PDR: NVD on or within 1 disc diameter ≥ ETDRS standard photo 10A (~one-quarter to one-third disc area) ± vitreous/preretinal haemorrhage; OR vitreous/preretinal haemorrhage with new vessels (NVD < 10A, or NVE ≥ one-quarter disc area) — Appendix 5 Table A5-1
audit.reason: Appendix 5 Table A5-1 (p.P134) verbatim: 'New vessels on or within 1 disc diameter of the optic disc ≥ standard photograph 10A* (about one-quarter to one-third disc area), with or without vitreous or preretinal hemorrhage; or vitreous and/or preretinal hemorrhage accompanied by new vessels, either new vessels at the optic disc < standard photograph 10A or new vessels elsewhere ≥ one-quarter disc area.' The disc-area threshold, both limbs of the OR, and the < / ≥ directions are all correct. Table credit line verified: 'ETDRS report number 7. Ophthalmology 1991;98:742' — matches the finding's citation exactly.

audit.assertion: ICDR derived from ETDRS + WESDR by modified Delphi at an April 2002 workshop (International Congress of Ophthalmology), Global Diabetic Retinopathy Project Task Force; explicitly not a replacement for ETDRS
audit.reason: Cited AAO clinical-statement URL fetched and live; it is dated 'May 2012', is attributed to the 'Global Diabetic Retinopathy Project Task Force and Invitational Workshop', and contains verbatim 'an evidence-based approach, namely the findings of the Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) and the Wisconsin Epidemiologic Study of Diabetic Retinopathy (WESDR)', 'A modified Delphi technique was utilized', 'A workshop was held in April 2002 in conjunction with the International Congress of Ophthalmology', and 'This would not replace the ETDRS, but provide a common, user-friendly terminology'. I specifically probed the '(summary document dated October 2002)' parenthetical, suspecting a fabricated date: the cited page carries only 'May 2012'. However the underlying AAO summary asset does exist and is headed 'October 2002 — SUMMARY: INTERNATIONAL CLINICAL DIABETIC RETINOPATHY AND DIABETIC MACULAR EDEMA DISEASE SEVERITY SCALES', at https://www.aao.org/Assets/3d3ce31b-39cf-444e-b393-1ae0ca8bfcf9/634965436738770000/sum-clinical-dr-and-dme-pdf (HTTP 200, 99,142 bytes), and it contains every claimed element verbatim including the 30-member task-force roster. The parenthetical is therefore accurate but points at a second document; adding that URL would make the citation self-contained.
audit.correctedSource: AAO clinical statement 'International Clinical Classification System for Diabetic Retinopathy and Diabetic Macular Edema', May 2012 — the October 2002 summary is a separate linked asset: https://www.aao.org/Assets/3d3ce31b-39cf-444e-b393-1ae0ca8bfcf9/634965436738770000/sum-clinical-dr-and-dme-pdf

audit.assertion: ETDRS classification levels (mild/moderate/severe NPDR, early PDR, high-risk PDR) per AAO PPP Appendix 5 Table A5-1, from ETDRS report 7 (Ophthalmology 1991;98:742) with grading per ETDRS report 10 (Ophthalmology 1991;98:786-806)
audit.reason: Table A5-1 extracted verbatim and every level matches, including the intricate severe-NPDR rule: 'Cotton wool spots, venous beading, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities all definitely present in at least two of fields 4 through 7; or 2 of the preceding 3 lesions present in at least two of fields 4 through 7 and hemorrhages and microaneurysms present in these 4 fields, ≥ standard photo 2A in at least one of them; or intraretinal microvascular abnormalities present in each of fields 4 through 7 and ≥ standard photograph 8A in at least two of them.' Mild ('At least 1 microaneurysm, and definition not met for moderate...') and early PDR ('New vessels; definition not met for high-risk proliferative retinopathy') also match. Both ETDRS citations verified as the table's own credit lines: report 7 at 'Ophthalmology 1991;98:742' and report 10 at 'Ophthalmology 1991;98:786-806' (the latter also appears in the Glossary reprint credit).

audit.assertion: ICO 2017 Table 1 DME grading: no DME; non-central-involved DME (thickening not involving the 1 mm central subfield); central-involved DME (thickening involving the 1 mm central subfield)
audit.reason: URL fetched by me: HTTP 200, 5,605,544-byte PDF; front matter 'ICO Guidelines for Diabetic Eye Care, Updated 2017' and 'Copyright © ICO January 2017' — version and date exactly as cited. Table 1 DME rows verbatim: 'No DME — No retinal thickening or hard exudates in the macula'; 'Noncentral-involved DME — Retinal thickening in the macula that does not involve the central subfield zone that is 1mm in diameter'; 'Central-involved DME — Retinal thickening in the macula that does involve the central subfield zone that is 1mm in diameter'. Two caveats, neither affecting the values: (1) the sourceUrl is a third-party mirror (vrsp.org.ph, a Philippine retina society), not ICO's own site — I tested ICO's own download path (icoph.org/downloads/ICOGuidelinesforDiabeticEyeCare.pdf) and it now returns 404, so the mirror is a defensible fallback, but under the 'prefer the standard-setting body's own page' rule this should be recorded as a secondary host; (2) the contextual clause 'rather than the original 2003 mild/moderate/severe scale' is NOT verified — the October 2002 AAO summary I fetched contains no DME severity table, and I did not confirm the 2003 mild/moderate/severe DME wording in any retrieved document. Treat that clause as background, not sourced.

audit.assertion: AAO PPP 2024 Table 2: type 1 first exam 5 years after diagnosis then yearly; type 2 at diagnosis then yearly; pregnancy soon after conception/early first trimester, then 3-12 months (no DR to moderate NPDR) or 1-3 months (severe NPDR or worse); gestational diabetes needs no exam in pregnancy
audit.reason: Table 2 (p.P93) verbatim: 'Type 1 — 5 years after diagnosis — Yearly'; 'Type 2 — At time of diagnosis — Yearly'; 'Pregnancy (type 1 or type 2) — Soon after conception and early in the first trimester — No retinopathy to mild or moderate NPDR: every 3–12 months; Severe NPDR or worse: every 1–3 months'; footnote ‡ verbatim: 'Women who develop gestational diabetes do not require an eye examination during pregnancy and do not appear to be at increased risk for DR during pregnancy.' All intervals, both diabetes types and the gestational footnote are exactly right. Worth logging as a conflict for the tool: this yearly interval sits alongside finding 25's WHO PEN biennial interval, and the two findings do not cross-reference each other.

audit.assertion: ICO 2017 Tables 2a/2b resource-stratified re-examination and referral intervals by ICDR grade
audit.reason: Both tables extracted verbatim and every one of the 14 cells matches. Table 2a (high resource): no apparent DR/mild NPDR with no DME 1-2 year, no referral; mild NPDR 6-12 months, no referral; moderate NPDR 3-6 months, referral required; severe NPDR <3 months, referral required; PDR <1 month, referral required; noncentral-involved DME 3 months, referral required; central-involved DME 1 month, referral required. Table 2b (low/intermediate): identical except mild NPDR 1-2 year (no referral), moderate NPDR 6-12 months (referral required), and noncentral-involved DME 3 months with 'Referral not required (referral recommended if laser resources available)' — the finding reproduced even that parenthetical correctly. One pedantic note: Table 2b is titled 'Based on Simplified Classification of Diabetic Retinopathy', not 'International Classification' as in Table 2a, so describing both as 'keyed to the ICDR grade' is slightly loose for 2b.

audit.assertion: AAO PPP 2024 Table 5 follow-up months (no DME / NCI-DME / CI-DME): no apparent DR 12/–/–; mild NPDR 12/3-6/1; moderate NPDR 6-12/3-6/1; severe NPDR 3-4/2-4/1; non-high-risk PDR 3-4/2-4/1; high-risk PDR 2-4/2-4/1
audit.reason: Table 5 extracted verbatim; all 16 follow-up values match exactly, including that 'No apparent retinopathy' has only a no-DME row (12 months) with no NCI/CI entries, and that CI-DME is uniformly 1 month across every severity. Minor descriptive note: the table's actual title is 'INITIAL MANAGEMENT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR PATIENTS WITH DIABETES' — the finding describes it as follow-up intervals, which is the content of its 'Follow-up (Months)' column but not the table's name. The moderate-NPDR/no-DME cell carries a footnote marker ('6–12‡') that the finding omits.

audit.assertion: WHO PEN 2020: dilated-pupil retinal exam at diagnosis then every 2 years, or as per ophthalmologist recommendation
audit.reason: WHO PEN 2020 p.25, section '2.2 DIABETES / SCREENING FOR CHRONIC COMPLICATIONS', verbatim: 'REFER for dilated-pupil retinal exam upon diagnosis and every 2 years thereafter, or as per ophthalmologist recommendation.' Corroborated in the second cited source, the WHO PEN training manual: '...trained person upon diagnosis and every 2 years thereafter'. Both documents fetched by me (HTTP 200). Both cited sources genuinely carry the claim.

bundle.domain: Diabetic foot and peripheral neuropathy — IWGDF 2023 risk stratification, LOPS testing, PAD assessment, and ulcer classification (SINBAD / WIfI)

findings.assertion: IWGDF risk category 0 (very low ulcer risk) is defined as no loss of protective sensation and no signs of peripheral artery disease, and is screened annually.
findings.value: Category 0 = no LOPS AND no signs of PAD; screening frequency once a year
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Table 1); current as of Sept 2026 — next update due at ISDF May 2027
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines on the prevention and management of diabetes-related foot disease (2023 update), Table 1
findings.quote: 0 Very low No LOPS and no signs of PAD Once a year
findings.notes: Retrieved the PDF from the IWGDF site and extracted text locally. Annual screening for risk 0 is a Strong/High GRADE recommendation in the companion Prevention Guideline (Recommendation 1).

findings.assertion: IWGDF risk category 1 (low ulcer risk) is defined by the presence of either loss of protective sensation or peripheral artery disease, screened every 6-12 months.
findings.value: Category 1 = LOPS OR PAD; screening frequency once every 6-12 months
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Table 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Table 1
findings.quote: 1 Low LOPS or PAD Once every 6-12 months
findings.notes: Either finding alone moves the patient from 'not at risk' to 'at-risk', which triggers the more comprehensive foot examination described in section 3.2.

findings.assertion: IWGDF risk category 2 (moderate ulcer risk) requires a combination of two of LOPS, PAD and foot deformity, screened every 3-6 months.
findings.value: Category 2 = (LOPS + PAD) OR (LOPS + foot deformity) OR (PAD + foot deformity); screening frequency once every 3-6 months
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Table 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Table 1
findings.quote: 2 Moderate LOPS + PAD, or LOPS + foot deformity or PAD + foot deformity Once every 3-6 months
findings.notes: Note the logic: deformity alone does not qualify — it must be paired with LOPS or PAD. Foot deformity is not numerically defined in Table 1; the guideline gives examples (claw/hammer toes, abnormally large bony prominences, limited joint mobility) in section 3.2.

findings.assertion: IWGDF risk category 3 (high ulcer risk) requires LOPS or PAD plus at least one of prior foot ulcer, prior lower-extremity amputation, or end-stage renal disease, screened every 1-3 months.
findings.value: Category 3 = (LOPS OR PAD) AND >=1 of: history of a foot ulcer; lower-extremity amputation (minor or major); end-stage renal disease. Screening frequency once every 1-3 months
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Table 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Table 1
findings.quote: 3 High LOPS or PAD, and one or more of the following: - history of a foot ulcer - a lower-extremity amputation (minor or major) - end-stage renal disease
findings.notes: The guideline separately states a person with a healed foot ulcer has the highest risk and 'the foot should be considered in remission', requiring lifelong prevention strategies.

findings.assertion: The IWGDF screening intervals attached to each risk category are expert opinion, not evidence-derived, and should be presented as such in any decision-support tool.
findings.value: All four screening intervals (annual / 6-12 mo / 3-6 mo / 1-3 mo) carry an explicit expert-opinion caveat
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Table 1 footnote)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Table 1 footnote
findings.quote: * Screening frequency is based on expert opinion, since there is no published evidence to support these intervals
findings.notes: Important for a decision-support surface: the risk stratification itself rests on high-certainty evidence (LOPS and PAD predict ulceration), but the intervals do not. ADA reproduces the same caveat.

findings.assertion: The ADA independently adopts the IWGDF risk stratification system unchanged, which corroborates the four categories and their screening frequencies.
findings.value: ADA Table 12.1 reproduces categories 0-3 with identical criteria and frequencies (annual / 6-12 mo / 3-6 mo / 1-3 mo)
findings.standardVersion: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024, Section 12; Diabetes Care 47(Suppl 1):S231–S243
findings.sourceTitle: 12. Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024 (American Diabetes Association)
findings.quote: International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot risk stratification system and corresponding foot screening frequency … Adapted with permission from Schaper et al.
findings.notes: Cross-standard agreement on stratification. I fetched the 2024 edition only — I did not verify the 2025 or 2026 ADA editions.

findings.assertion: Loss of protective sensation is formally defined by IWGDF as a sign of peripheral neuropathy, an inability to sense light pressure such as that applied by a 10 g Semmes-Weinstein monofilament.
findings.value: LOPS = inability to sense light pressure, exemplar stimulus 10 g (5.07) Semmes-Weinstein monofilament
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update — Definitions and criteria for diabetes-related foot disease
findings.sourceTitle: Definitions and criteria for diabetes-related foot disease (IWGDF 2023 update), van Netten et al., Diabetes Metab Res Rev
findings.quote: Loss of protective sensation: A sign of peripheral neuropathy, characterised by an inability to sense light pressure, for example, as applied with a 10 g Semmes‐Weinstein monofilament.
findings.notes: Definition is qualitative — there is no numeric cut-point beyond the 10 g filament force itself.

findings.assertion: The IWGDF 10 g monofilament technique requires testing three different sites on both feet, applied perpendicular to the skin with enough force to buckle the filament, over a total approach-contact-removal time of about 2 seconds.
findings.value: 3 sites per foot; 10 g (5.07) filament; perpendicular application to buckling; total duration approx. 2 seconds
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 1: Doing a sensory foot examination
findings.quote: Test three different sites on both feet, selecting from those shown in Figure 4. … The total duration of the approach -> skin contact -> and removal of the filament should be approximately 2 seconds.
findings.notes: Also mandated: demonstrate on hand/elbow/forehead first; patient must not see the application; do not apply over ulcer, callus, scar or necrotic tissue; do not slide the filament or make repetitive contact at a site.

findings.assertion: IWGDF monofilament scoring uses three questions per site (two real applications alternating with at least one mock application), with a 2-out-of-3 rule.
findings.value: Protective sensation present = 2/3 correct answers at that site; absent = 2/3 incorrect answers
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 1
findings.quote: Protective sensation is: present at each site if the patient correctly answers on two out of three applications; absent with two out of three incorrect answers.
findings.notes: The patient is asked both whether they feel pressure ('yes'/'no') and where they feel it. The mock application is a required distractor, not optional.

findings.assertion: The IWGDF monofilament test sites are shown only as a diagram (Figure 4), which marks three plantar points per foot — the hallux and two metatarsal head regions — with no text labels.
findings.value: Figure 4 shows 3 marked plantar sites per foot: plantar hallux, first metatarsal head region, fifth metatarsal head region
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Figure 4, page 25)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Figure 4
findings.quote: Figure 4: Sites that should be tested for loss of protective sensation with the 10g Semmes-Weinstein monofilament
findings.notes: IMPORTANT PROVENANCE CAVEAT: I retrieved the PDF and rendered page 25 to an image to read the figure, but the figure carries NO anatomical text labels. The anatomical naming above is my reading of the drawn circles, not wording from IWGDF. A CSO must confirm the site labels before they are hard-coded into a data model.

findings.assertion: IWGDF specifies monofilament maintenance intervals because filaments lose buckling force with use.
findings.value: Rest the filament 24 hours after assessing 10-15 patients; replace after use on 70-90 patients
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 1
findings.quote: we suggest not using the monofilament for the next 24 hours after assessing 10-15 patients and replacing it after using it on 70-90 patients
findings.notes: Guideline hedges with 'Depending on the type of monofilament'. Highly relevant to a low-resource deployment where filaments may be reused far beyond this.

findings.assertion: The 128 Hz tuning fork is applied to a bony part of the dorsal side of the distal phalanx of the hallux, with a 2-out-of-3 scoring rule including a mock application.
findings.value: 128 Hz; site = bony dorsal distal phalanx of first toe (or another toe if hallux absent); positive if >=2/3 correct, negative if 2/3 incorrect
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 1
findings.quote: Apply the tuning fork to a bony part on the dorsal side of the distal phalanx of the first toe (or another toe if the hallux is absent). … The test is positive if the patient correctly answers at least two out of three applications
findings.notes: If vibration is not sensed at the toe, IWGDF directs repeating the test more proximally (e.g. malleolus, tibial tuberosity). Note the tuning fork detects loss of vibratory sensation; the monofilament is the test that detects LOPS proper.

findings.assertion: The Ipswich Touch Test is the IWGDF-endorsed fallback when neither monofilament nor tuning fork is available: light index-finger touch to the tips of the first, third and fifth toes of both feet for 1-2 seconds.
findings.value: Sites = tips of 1st, 3rd and 5th toes bilaterally (6 sites); contact 1-2 seconds; LOPS likely when light touch is not sensed at >=2 sites
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 1)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 1: Light touch test
findings.quote: The examiner lightly sequentially touches with the tip of hers/his index finger the tips of the first, third, and fifth toes of both feet for 1–2 s … LOPS is likely when light touch is not sensed in ≥ 2 sites
findings.notes: Directly relevant to a Ugandan deployment. IWGDF explicitly limits the claim: 'The test has reasonable agreement with these tests to determine LOPS, but its accuracy in predicting foot ulcers has not been established.' Do not present it as equivalent to the monofilament for ulcer risk prediction. Also: do not push, tap or poke.

findings.assertion: IWGDF 2023 endorses a biothesiometer/neurothesiometer as a second-line vibration screen but publishes NO numeric vibration perception threshold for it.
findings.value: No volt threshold stated anywhere in the IWGDF 2023 documents I retrieved (the commonly cited >25 V cut-off is NOT in these documents)
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Prevention Guideline, Recommendation 1 rationale)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Guidelines on the prevention of foot ulcers in persons with diabetes (2023 update)
findings.quote: we suggest to screen for this with a tuning fork or biothesiometer/neurothesiometer, if outcomes from monofilament testing do not show LOPS
findings.notes: NEGATIVE FINDING, deliberately reported. I grepped all five retrieved IWGDF 2023 PDFs (Practical, Prevention, Classification, PAD, Definitions) for 'biothesiomet', 'neurothesiomet', 'volt', 'VPT', 'vibration perception threshold': the only hit is the sentence quoted. Do NOT encode a 25 V threshold citing IWGDF. Note also the sequencing: vibration testing is positioned as an ADD-ON when monofilament testing does NOT show LOPS.

findings.assertion: IWGDF requires at least annual pedal pulse palpation and PAD history in every person with diabetes without a foot ulcer.
findings.value: History + inspection for ischaemia + pedal pulse palpation, at least annually or with any change in foot clinical status (Strong, Low)
findings.standardVersion: 2023 intersocietal IWGDF/ESVS/SVS PAD Guideline, Recommendation 1
findings.sourceTitle: The intersocietal IWGDF, ESVS, SVS guidelines on peripheral artery disease in people with diabetes and a foot ulcer (2023 update)
findings.quote: In a person with diabetes without a foot ulcer, take a relevant history for peripheral artery disease, examine the foot for signs of ischaemia and palpate the foot pulses at least annually, or with any change in clinical status of the feet. (Strong, Low)
findings.notes: Guideline is explicit that pulse palpation is weak in isolation (PLR only 1.84-2.46 for an absent/weak pulse) and that neuropathy can mask claudication while autonomic neuropathy can produce a warm foot — so a palpable pulse does not exclude PAD.

findings.assertion: IWGDF states no single non-invasive test diagnoses or excludes PAD, but gives a combination of values that make PAD less likely.
findings.value: PAD less likely if ABI 0.9-1.3 AND TBI >=0.70 AND triphasic or biphasic pedal Doppler waveforms. No value excludes PAD.
findings.standardVersion: 2023 intersocietal IWGDF/ESVS/SVS PAD Guideline, Recommendations 2 and 4
findings.sourceTitle: Intersocietal IWGDF/ESVS/SVS PAD Guideline (2023 update)
findings.quote: No single modality has been shown to be optimal for the diagnosis of PAD, and there is no value above which PAD can be excluded. However, PAD is less likely in the presence of ABI 0.9-1.3; TBI ≥ 0.70; and triphasic or biphasic pedal Doppler waveforms.
findings.notes: Recommendation 2 (no ulcer) is Conditional/Low; Recommendation 4 (with ulcer or gangrene) is Strong/Low — same numbers, different strength. Any UI must not present these as a rule-out.

findings.assertion: An ABI above 1.3 or below 0.9 is abnormal and indicative of PAD.
findings.value: ABI >1.3 or <0.9 = abnormal (indicative of PAD); ABI 0.9-1.3 = normal range
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 2)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 2
findings.quote: An ABI above 1.3 or below 0.9 is abnormal, i.e. indicative of PAD
findings.notes: ABI is a dimensionless ratio — no SI/conventional unit duality applies. The high value (>1.3) reflects medial arterial calcification, which is common in diabetes and renal disease and makes ABI falsely reassuring.

findings.assertion: IWGDF recommends a diabetes-specific ABI calculation using the LOWER of the dorsalis pedis / posterior tibial pressures, which differs from the traditional method using the higher pressure.
findings.value: IWGDF method: ABI = lower of (dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial) pressure of that foot / highest of (left, right) brachial pressure. Traditional method uses the higher pedal pressure.
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 2)
findings.sourceTitle: IWGDF Practical Guidelines (2023 update), Appendix 2: Calculation of ABI in persons with diabetes
findings.quote: calculate the ankle-brachial index (ABI) for each limb by dividing the lower value of the dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial pressures of that foot by the highest of the left or right brachial pressures … The ABI has traditionally been calculated using the higher of the dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial pressures. This gives a best-case scenario of blood flow to the foot.
findings.notes: CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. The rationale is below-knee disease affecting only one tibial artery. Any ABI calculator must state which convention it uses, because the two produce different numbers on the same patient. See conflicts.

findings.assertion: A toe-brachial index below 0.70 is abnormal and indicative of PAD.
findings.value: TBI <0.70 = abnormal (indicative of PAD); TBI >=0.70 supports PAD being less likely
findings.standardVersion: 2023 update (Practical Guidelines, Appendix 2)
